author: Times News
description:
“They’ve basically got the best possible person, designed in a lab, to prove that to themselves, Andy Burnham.”

If Andy Burnham loses in Makerfield, it may become unclear who the Labour Party is for, says The Sunday Times associate editor Josh Glancy.

Josh Glancy was speaking to Ayesha Hazarika on Times Radio Weekend Drive. Listen live every Saturday and Sunday from 4-7pm.

description:
“This is another pot that America is stirring with no certainty as to the outcome.”

description:
“If this has finally prompted him to wake up from this stupor, then I’ll take the win.”

Starmer has finally seen “what is painfully and scarily obvious to all of us”: that the world has become extremely dangerous, and £18 billion is a “decent sum of money”, says former Downing Street director of communications for Boris Johnson, Guto Harri.

Guto Harri and Rebecca Hutson were speaking to Rosie Wright and Calum Macdonald on Times Radio Breakfast. Listen live every day from 6–10am.

author: Times News
description:
“I’m afraid this is pure and raw politics.”

The £18 billion Starmer has pledged to defence spending is welcome, but “it’s not enough”, “doesn’t go far enough” and has only come “now his own job is on the line”, says former Chief of the General Staff and head of the British Army, General Lord Dannatt.

General Lord Dannatt was speaking to Rosie Wright and Calum Macdonald on Times Radio Breakfast. Listen live every day from 6–10am.

author: Times News
description:
“Winning a parliamentary by-election… does not a platform make.”

Cabinet ministers are reportedly calling for Streeting and Starmer to “stand aside” if Burnham wins the Makerfield by-election, but history shows that “an internal debate would benefit and strengthen” whoever wins, says political strategist and founder of Lowick-Hedry, Kevin McKeever.

Kevin McKeever was speaking to Rosie Wright and Calum Macdonald on Times Radio Breakfast. Listen live every day from 6–10am.
